title: Existence of the two normalized finite comparisons
statement: Let d be an adic coefficient datum and sq a cartesian square with open horizontal arrows. In the strict completed-ring and finite constant-ring coordinates [def-cbc-completed-finite-exchange-coordinates], there exist natural source and target finite-comparison isomorphisms satisfying respectively CbcSourceFiniteNormalization and CbcTargetFiniteNormalization [def-cbc-finite-comparison-models], on every K-flat representative, with no boundedness, completeness or quasi-compactness condition. This statement asserts existence only.

source.place: Finite-exchange/reduction identification before Rlim; Stacks 03DI, sites-modules.tex, lemma-extension-by-zero; completed-ring strict exchange is an agent-written refinement.

proof.text: The canonical completed coefficient map is invertible by the compatible inverse-image comparison for finite profinite coefficient towers. Scalar restriction along that isomorphism is an equivalence. Its inverse is ordinary scalar extension by uniqueness of left adjoints. Pro-etale module inverse image is exact, hence completed module pullback and its termwise strict-tower functor are exact. A universal left-derived counit of this exact functor is invertible everywhere by the localization universal property. This uses the existing completedCoefficient_isIso proof and proves the exactness and counit consequences privately in the item.

Compose the actual reduction, exact open-extension, tower-pullback and exact-evaluation counits, in source and target order, as natural transformations on complexes. Postcompose with the localized ordinary coordinate isomorphisms cbcSourceLevel and cbcTargetLevel. For each finite endpoint compose the scalar-extension counit with the exact scalar-restriction and finite source/target localization factors. Every resulting model map is invertible on K-flat complexes: use the reduction and scalar-extension computation properties, Step 1, and exact localization factors. These are natural transformations with the precise original model components.

The generic private descentComparison lemma passes natural model maps through the homotopy quotient using fullness of precomposition. Restrict to the full homotopy subcategory represented by K-flat complexes. Every homotopy object admits a denominator from this subcategory by K-flat resolutions. The resolving-subcategory localization lemma restriction_localization (already proved in SiteDerivedTensorDescentIndependentCoefficients) identifies its localization with the whole derived category. On this subcategory divide the first model comparison by the second; both are invertible. Lift this natural isomorphism through localization. The lift factorization, followed by naturality for quotientCompQhIso and cancellation, gives the model equation on every K-flat complex.

Apply the generic descentFourComparison lemma separately to the source and target counits of Step 2. Its conclusion explicitly retains the nested four-stage source formula and the two-stage finite model formula. Thus no concrete reassociation of complex-functor objects is required. Expanding the named representative maps identifies the two resulting equations with exactly CbcSourceFiniteNormalization and CbcTargetFiniteNormalization. Both specified finite comparison isomorphisms exist, without a boundedness, completeness, quasi-compactness, nonzero-ring or nonempty-scheme hypothesis.

lean.statement:
theorem cbcNormalizedFiniteComparison_exists (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ e : completedReductionTower U d ⋙ cbcStrictOpen d j sq.isOpenImmersion ⋙
          completedTowerPullback g d ⋙ pbcTowerEvaluation X' (pbcAdicCompletion X' d) n ≅
        cbcFiniteReduction d U n ⋙ (cbcFiniteSource d sq n).mapDerivedCategory,
      CbcSourceFiniteNormalization d sq n e) ∧
    (∃ e : completedReductionTower U d ⋙ completedTowerPullback gU d ⋙
          cbcStrictOpen d j' sq.isOpenImmersion' ⋙
            pbcTowerEvaluation X' (pbcAdicCompletion X' d) n ≅
        cbcFiniteReduction d U n ⋙ (cbcFiniteTarget d sq n).mapDerivedCategory,
      CbcTargetFiniteNormalization d sq n e)
